brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Build Your Professional Portfolio with ChatGPT Sites

questions.question: What are the four key deliverables you will have by the end of this course?
choices: Portfolio Site, Personal Positioning, Case Study, and AI Assistant
Resume, LinkedIn Profile, Cover Letter, and Job Applications
Website Design, Content Writing, Video Production, and Photography
Business Plan, Marketing Strategy, Financial Projections, and Pitch Deck
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—these four deliverables represent your complete toolkit for a professional online presence.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course focuses on building specific portfolio assets using ChatGPT Sites. Review Slide 2 to see the four core deliverables you'll create.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the core question your portfolio must answer?
choices: How much money can you make?
Why should this person be trusted with important work?
What is your educational background?
How many years of experience do you have?
questions.feedback_correct: You've got it—trust is the foundation of every strong portfolio, and you need to establish it within 30 seconds.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Portfolio Promise isn't about credentials alone—it's about demonstrating trustworthiness. Review Slide 9 to understand what truly matters to visitors.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a portfolio and a résumé?
choices: A portfolio is longer and more detailed than a résumé
A résumé lists experience, while a portfolio provides proof with context and results
A portfolio is only for creative professionals, while a résumé is for everyone
A résumé is digital, while a portfolio is always printed
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—proof and context transform a simple list of duties into a compelling narrative about your impact.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The difference isn't about length or format. A portfolio tells the story of what changed because of your work, with evidence. See Slide 8 for clarification.

questions.question: Before you start building your portfolio site with ChatGPT, what should you do first?
choices: Immediately open ChatGPT Sites and start writing
Gather your raw materials like résumé, LinkedIn bio, project samples, and testimonials
Hire a professional web designer to plan the layout
Research your competitors' portfolio sites for inspiration
questions.feedback_correct: You're prepared—gathering your materials first ensures ChatGPT has the best information to work with and speeds up the build.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes gathering what you already have before building. You likely have everything needed. Check Slide 5 for the full list of materials to collect.

questions.question: According to Slide 7, what should you do immediately after your portfolio site first appears?
choices: Start editing and redesigning everything you see
Ask five critical review questions before making any changes
Publish it immediately to get feedback from visitors
Delete sections that don't match your original vision
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—stepping back for objective evaluation prevents wasted edits and helps you focus on what actually matters.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The instinct to immediately edit can lead to unnecessary changes. Slide 7 teaches you to pause and ask diagnostic questions first.

questions.question: What are the three focused passes recommended in the Mini Activity for editing your portfolio?
choices: Design, Content, and Publishing
Clarify the message, Improve the layout, and Strengthen the proof
Grammar, Spelling, and Punctuation
Add visuals, Remove text, and Update links
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified the three strategic passes that build on each other to create a polished, functional portfolio.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The three-pass edit focuses on meaning and function, not just mechanics. Review Slide 12 to understand each pass's specific goal.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a benchmark for a strong first portfolio site?
choices: Easy to Scan and Audience-Aware
Specific and Honest
Evidence-Based and Visually stunning with professional graphics
Clear Next Steps
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the course teaches that a strong portfolio needs to be clear and functional, not necessarily flashy or graphics-heavy.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 13 lists six benchmarks for a strong portfolio, and visual complexity isn't among them. Focus on clarity over decoration.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the purpose of using a prompt to get feedback on your portfolio before making changes?
choices: To make you feel confident about your work
To identify what is holding your portfolio back and prioritize improvements by impact
To find a professional designer who can rebuild your site
To get permission from an expert before publishing
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—diagnosis comes before treatment, which prevents wasted effort on low-impact changes.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The feedback step isn't about validation or permission—it's about strategic diagnosis. Slide 10 shows how to identify what matters most before editing.

questions.question: The course emphasizes that a portfolio should clearly communicate three core elements about you. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
choices: Who you help (your target audience)
What problems you solve
How much you charge for your services
How you work (your process and approach)
questions.feedback_correct: Right—Slide 3 identifies the three core elements of your portfolio's message, and pricing strategy is not one of them.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 3 outlines the Big Idea behind portfolio messaging. Review those three core elements: who you help, what problems you solve, and how you work.

questions.question: How does the course suggest approaching the challenge of making your portfolio stand out from AI-generated content?
choices: Avoid using ChatGPT Sites and build your site manually instead
Use Section 1 to build a first version quickly, then Section 2 teaches you to personalize it and make it distinctly yours
Add more complex graphics and animations to distract from AI writing
Copy content from successful competitors' portfolios
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the course acknowledges that the first version is AI-generated and intentionally teaches personalization in the full course.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course's strategy is to build fast first, then personalize. Slide 14 and 15 reveal that making it distinctly yours is the work of Section 2 and beyond.
